cohort: The study included offspring of parous women where one sibling was prenatally exposed to maternal preeclampsia and the other was not.
finding: Offspring born following pregnancies complicated with preeclampsia were at a significantly higher risk (HR 1.324, 95% CI 1.168-1.503) for long-term infectious hospitalization compared to offspring of mothers without preeclampsia, even after adjusting for confounders.
